findings.quote: principal or managed policy, that purges content per room and provenance class
findings.problem: A retention policy purges by room and provenance class with no exemption for pins that restore (device-seat pins are `operator`, run-seat pins `assistant`), and Purge says every act keeps its effect after its free text is purged. A managed policy alone can therefore leave a constraint that still qualifies but has no text, which breaks I3 (restored verbatim, or named by id and count only when the budget omits it) and gives no rule that counts the loss (I6).
findings.fix: Add to Retention policy: it never purges the text of a pin that restores; only the principal's explicit purge does, and a restore block then names a pin whose text was purged by id and count.

findings.quote: turning off restore blocks or lowering the pin budget, which take effect
findings.problem: The relative clause 'which take effect without acceptance' has no clear antecedent. It can mean repository configuration's cut-only changes need no acceptance, which differs from the preceding Record rule that even cut-only configuration changes wait for acceptance. It can also be read as applying to the very changes the sentence forbids. Two implementers could build different acceptance behaviour for `.parinn.toml`.
findings.fix: Reword: '...pin budget; the cut-only changes it does make take effect without acceptance (ADM-04).'
